finding.claim: SQL injection in ORDER BY: the unsanitized `sort` GET parameter is concatenated directly into the query string. An attacker can inject subqueries or CASE-based boolean/blind expressions (e.g. sort=(CASE WHEN (SELECT substr(...)) ... END)) to exfiltrate data from any table in the SQLite DB. Prepared statements are not used for this one.
finding.sink: $pdo->query("SELECT id, name FROM users ORDER BY " . $sort) at list.php:6

trace.note: concatenated into SQL and executed via PDO::query

finding.guards_checked: No allowlist, casting, or escaping in list_users_sorted. The sibling list_users_safe (line 10-12) uses an allowlist map and find_user (line 16) uses a bound parameter; both are safe and not reported.

verdict.guard_found: none in list_users_sorted; the allowlist at list.php:10-11 and the bound parameter at list.php:16 only protect the other functions
verdict.reason: list.php:5-6 takes $_GET['sort'] with no validation and concatenates it into the ORDER BY clause that PDO::query executes. Nothing in the file calls list_users_sorted or gates access to it, so I could not confirm from this file who can reach it.
